title: Putnami Scope Configuration
description: Scope-level configuration file (putnami.json). Placed in intermediate directories between workspace root and projects. Defines inheritable config (tags, extensions, publishConfig) and optionally declares included sub-projects. When `activate: true`, the same file also acts as a project — project-shape fields (name, type, options, jobs, dependencies, etc.) are accepted and apply to the scope-self project.

line.description: Declares this scope a version line: its projects are versioned and tagged together, and their version is derived from the line's git tags. A project belongs to its nearest ancestor line, exactly one; a line under another line, or a line on an activated scope, is a validation error. A workspace where no scope declares a line is one line, with the pattern 'v{version}'.

tag.description: Pattern of the line's git tags, carrying exactly one '{version}' placeholder and otherwise made of [A-Za-z0-9._/{}-] (for example 'ts/v{version}'). Omitted means the default '<scope path>/v{version}'.

activate.description: When true, the scope directory is also registered as an activation target — extensions run against the scope itself in addition to its declared includes. Use this for scope-shaped artifacts (e.g. workspace-level infra) that don't fit a leaf project.

includes.description: Included project paths relative to this scope directory. Makes this an autonomous scope that declares its own sub-projects.

tags.description: Tags inherited by all projects under this scope. Merged (union) with ancestor scope tags. When activate is true, also applied to the scope-self project.

extensions.description: Extensions inherited by all projects under this scope. Deepest scope wins (replaces, not merges). When activate is true, also applied to the scope-self project.

publishConfig.description: Publish configuration inherited by projects. Deepest scope wins per channel.

projectAliases.description: Project aliases (alias → target ID). Aggregated across all scopes; duplicates are an error.

groups.description: Project groups (group name → pattern). Aggregated across all scopes; duplicates are an error.

distribution.description: Distribution level inherited by every project under this scope that declares none of its own. Deepest scope wins. When activate is true, also applied to the scope-self project.

name.description: Project name for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

type.description: Project type for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

main.description: Main entry point for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

bin.description: Binary entry points for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

exports.description: Export map for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

publish.description: Publish channels for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

runsWith.description: Runtime service dependencies for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

build.description: Build configuration for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

dependencies.description: Workspace dependencies of the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

visibility.description: Import boundary of the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

registries.description: Registry entries overriding the workspace section for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

options.description: Per-command and per-extension parameter defaults applied to the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

jobs.description: Accepted but ignored, exactly as on a project: an activated scope is also a project, so a 'jobs' block here is parsed, warned about, and never planned. Use 'disable.jobs' or 'tasks' instead.

tasks.description: Per-task execution tuning for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

disable.description: Opt-out configuration for the scope-self project. Only meaningful when activate is true.

featureAuthority.description: Why this project declares no user-facing feature of its own. Set exactly one member. Absent means the project is expected to declare a feature.

owner.description: The authored feature ID this project contributes to, when the declaration lives in another project.

none.description: Why this project deliberately has no user-facing feature.
